title: Chilaquiles Verdes
description: Fried tortilla chips simmered briefly in a blended tomatillo-serrano salsa until just softened at the edges but still holding a little bite, then piled with crema, queso fresco, and a fried egg.

image.alt: Chilaquiles verdes topped with crumbled cheese, crema, and a fried egg

ingredients: 1/4 cup cilantro, plus more to serve
2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for frying
200g corn tortilla chips (or 8 corn tortillas, cut into wedges and fried)
steps: Boil the tomatillos and chilies in water for 8–10 minutes, until the tomatillos turn dull olive-green and soften. Drain.
Blend the tomatillos, chilies, half the onion, garlic, cilantro, and vegetable stock until smooth. Season with salt.
If frying your own tortillas: fry the wedges in oil until golden and crisp, then drain on paper towels.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet, pour in the salsa verde, and simmer 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the tortilla chips and toss gently to coat, cooking 1–2 minutes so they soften slightly but keep some crunch. Remove from heat.
Fry the eggs separately to your liking. Top the chilaquiles with the fried eggs, crema, queso fresco, remaining onion, and cilantro.
note: Add the chips off the heat or just before serving — they go from crisp to mush within a couple of minutes in the hot salsa.
